_comment: Create: Power Grid's own ingredients -> what Terra crafts them from instead (#172).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. ADR-0034's sweep is default-deny, so a Power Grid recipe ships only if
the pack authors it. `scripts/powergrid-recipe-convert.py` re-authors the 84 recipes the mod
puts on surfaces no block in this pack executes -- 43 `minecraft:crafting_shaped`, 28
`minecraft:crafting_shapeless` and 13 `create:mechanical_crafting`. The conversion is
mechanical (a pattern is flattened to an unordered ingredient list, counts preserved exactly),
and every judgement it makes is a row in this file rather than a branch in the script.
THE PROBLEM THIS FILE SOLVES. Power Grid is built for a Create pack, and Terra is not one.
ADR-0021 closes the input alphabet to iron, copper, coal and uranium plus stone and what the
surface grows, and cuts zinc outright with no exception -- which takes andesite alloy, andesite
casing, brass, the conductive casing and the shaft with it. ADR-0034 then removes every recipe
the pack does not author, so a vanilla item is obtainable only if it DROPS: glass, glass panes,
sticks, paper, terracotta and redstone are all grid-crafted and all gone, and even vanilla's
own `raw iron -> iron ingot` smelt is swept, which is why the ingot tags substitute and the
plate tags do not.
So the obtainable set is exactly: what a block drops, plus the outputs of the pack's own
emitted recipes. Every ingredient below is classified against that set and nothing else.
THE RULE: COUNTS ARE NEVER CHANGED. A substitution replaces an ingredient one-for-one at the
amount Power Grid asked for. Where that is lossy it is called out in the row's `reason` -- the
nugget rows are the loud case, since a nugget is a ninth of an ingot and its substitute is a
whole plate. Preserving the shape of the mod's own recipes was judged worth more than
re-costing 84 recipes by hand, and re-costing them is a later ticket's call, not this one's.
FIELDS.
`keep`        an ingredient that is already obtainable, passed through untouched. Every
entry names why it is obtainable, because 'it looks vanilla' is not a reason
under a default-deny sweep.
`substitute`  `to` is the replacement item, `reason` is the role being preserved.
`skip`        a recipe not emitted at all, and the pack recipe that already outputs it.
AN INGREDIENT IN NEITHER `keep` NOR `substitute` IS A HARD FAILURE, following
`item-map.json`'s rule: a name nobody has looked at must never be quietly passed through into
a recipe the player cannot craft. That is the whole failure this ticket was filed against.
`machine_only` is the second lever, and the reason `skip` is not used for the conversion rows.
Power Grid's `*_from_conversion` recipes turn a block into its other orientation, in BOTH
directions. Left as hand recipes they are three 2-cycles and three items with two routes, which
`RecipeGraph` resolves by taking whichever the recipe manager happened to hand it first -- 'an
arbitrary answer, not a stable one' -- and which `PlanResolver` has no cost model to escape.
Forcing them onto the machine takes them out of the Personal Assembler's graph entirely, so the
cycle cannot form, and BOTH directions still exist on the Assembling Machine. Skipping three of
them would have broken the cycle too, at the price of deleting the return trip from the game.

create:andesite_alloy.reason: Create's base structural alloy is andesite plus zinc, and ADR-0021 cuts zinc with no exception. Terra's base structural material is the iron plate, which is the role andesite alloy plays in every recipe here.

create:andesite_casing.reason: Andesite alloy again, one tier up. Same role, same substitute -- the pack has no casing item, and inventing one is ADR-0015's business rather than this converter's.

powergrid:conductive_casing.reason: An andesite casing plus a zinc ingot, so doubly out of alphabet. Its role is the conductive shell, and copper is Terra's conductor.

#c:plates/zinc.reason: Zinc is cut (ADR-0021). Copper is the pack's second plate and the electrical one, which is the role zinc plays in an electrical mod.

#c:ingots/zinc.reason: As above. The ingot form substitutes to the plate because no ingot is obtainable -- vanilla's raw-ore smelt is swept and only the pack's plate smelt survives.

#c:plates/brass.reason: Brass is copper plus zinc (ADR-0021 names it explicitly when cutting Create's Deployer). The copper half is the half Terra has.

#c:ingots/iron.reason: Not obtainable: vanilla `raw iron -> iron ingot` is a `minecraft:`-namespace smelt and the sweep removes it. The pack's iron plate is the surviving iron form.

#c:ingots/copper.reason: As the iron ingot row, for copper.

#c:nuggets/iron.reason: No nugget is obtainable -- the vanilla ingot-to-nugget recipe is a grid recipe and is swept. LOSSY: a nugget is a ninth of an ingot and this pays a whole plate for it. Re-costing is a later ticket's.

#c:nuggets/copper.reason: As the iron nugget row, and lossy in the same way. Vanilla has no copper nugget at all; the tag is Create's, whose items are swept too.

#c:wires/iron.reason: Power Grid's iron wire is made on a surface this ticket does not convert, so nothing produces it. The copper wire the pack already emits is the same role.

powergrid:copper_plating.reason: Made by a Create process the pack has no executor for. It is a copper sheet, which is what the pack's copper plate is.

powergrid:magnet.reason: `powergrid:magnetization` is the mod's own recipe type and this ticket does not admit that surface. A magnet is magnetised iron, so the iron plate is the honest stand-in.

powergrid:electrical_gizmo.reason: A sequenced-assembly item built on a zinc plate, so unreachable twice over. It is the mod's advanced electronic component and the pack's is the advanced circuit.

powergrid:transformer_core.reason: Made on a surface this ticket does not convert. A transformer core is laminated iron.

create:shaft.reason: Andesite alloy, so zinc-bearing. The pack emits an iron rod (`assembling/iron_stick.json`) and it is the same rotational-shaft role.

create:cogwheel.reason: Andesite alloy again. The pack emits an iron gear (`assembling/iron_gear_wheel.json`), which is Factorio's own name for the part.

create:clutch.reason: A brass-bearing Create component. Its role here is a geared coupling, which the iron gear covers.

create:encased_fan.reason: Andesite casing plus a shaft. Its role is the powered rotating assembly, which is what the pack's engine unit is.

create:precision_mechanism.reason: Brass, gold and cogs -- three separate reasons it cannot be made here. It is Create's high-tier precision component and the advanced circuit is the pack's.

create:display_board.reason: A Create block with no pack recipe. #148 already emits Power Grid's own display as Factorio's display panel, and it is the same part.

create:electron_tube.reason: Rose quartz plus an iron nugget; rose quartz is not on Terra. Its role is the basic electronic component, which is the electronic circuit.

create:polished_rose_quartz.reason: Rose quartz is a Create worldgen material and ADR-0021 closes the alphabet against it. It appears here only as electronics substrate.

create:cardboard.reason: Create makes it from dough, i.e. wheat, and its recipes are swept. Its role is a cheap sheet material and the pack's is the plastic bar (ADR-0025's chemistry emits it).

create:empty_schematic.reason: Paper plus a Create process. It appears once, as the substrate a circuit is printed on, so it takes the electronic circuit like the other substrates.

minecraft:redstone.reason: Redstone ore is not one of ADR-0021's four and nothing on Terra drops it. Every use here is as a conductor, which is the copper wire the pack already emits. #144's circuit-network split is the reason this does not silently become a circuit.

minecraft:comparator.reason: Redstone and quartz, both out of alphabet, and its own recipe is a swept grid recipe. It is a logic component.

minecraft:lever.reason: Craftable only on the vanilla grid, which no block executes (ADR-0034). Its role is a switch, which is a logic component here.

minecraft:compass.reason: Needs redstone, and its recipe is a swept grid recipe. It appears in the gauges, as their instrument movement.

minecraft:glass.reason: Sand smelts to glass on a `minecraft:`-namespace recipe, which the sweep removes -- only the pack's own smelts survive. The plastic bar is the pack's transparent-cover material.

minecraft:glass_pane.reason: Glass plus a swept grid recipe, so unobtainable twice. Same role and same substitute as glass.

minecraft:paper.reason: Sugar cane on a swept grid recipe. It is a sheet material here, not a book.

minecraft:terracotta.reason: Clay smelted on a swept `minecraft:` recipe. Its role is fired earthen block, and cobblestone is the obtainable stone Terra drops.

minecraft:stone_button.reason: A swept grid recipe. It is stone, and cobblestone is the stone that drops.

#minecraft:wooden_slabs.reason: A swept grid recipe. Logs are what Terra's surface actually grows (ADR-0016's Sapros trees).

minecraft:stick.reason: A swept grid recipe, and the pack has no wooden intermediate. Every use here is structural rather than fuel, so the iron rod is the role-preserving choice.

minecraft:dried_kelp.reason: Kelp is not part of what Terra's surface grows and the drying smelt is swept. It appears as Create's cardboard feedstock; logs are the obtainable organic material.

minecraft:potato.reason: Not part of Terra's surface growth (ADR-0021). Same organic-feedstock role as the kelp row.

minecraft:coal_block.reason: The compacting recipe is a swept grid recipe. Coal itself drops, so the block substitutes to the item -- LOSSY by a factor of nine, in the pack's favour.

minecraft:gold_nugget.reason: Gold is cut by ADR-0021's closed alphabet. It appears only as a contact material in electronics.

minecraft:lapis_lazuli.reason: Not one of Terra's four ores. It appears once, as electronics decoration.

minecraft:quartz.reason: Nether quartz, and #124 removed the Nether outright. Its role is the electronics substrate.

minecraft:amethyst_shard.reason: Amethyst geodes are not part of Terra's worldgen. It appears once, as a resonant electronics part.

minecraft:glowstone_dust.reason: Nether-only, and #124 removed the Nether. It appears in the indicator parts, where its role is the light-emitting element.

minecraft:diamond.reason: Not one of ADR-0021's four ores. It appears once and marks the most expensive part in its recipe, which is what the advanced circuit marks in the pack.

skip.alarm_bell: #148 already emits `assembling/programmable_speaker.json`, which outputs `powergrid:alarm_bell`. A second route would be a progression escape.

machine_only.voltage_gauge_from_conversion: One half of a 2-cycle with `current_gauge_from_conversion`, and a second route to `powergrid:voltage_gauge`, which `voltage_gauge` already makes.
machine_only.current_gauge_from_conversion: The other half. It is also the ONLY route to `powergrid:current_gauge`, which is why the pair moves to the machine rather than one of them being dropped.
machine_only.generator_housing_from_conversion: One half of a 2-cycle with `vertical_generator_housing_from_conversion`, and a second route to `powergrid:generator_housing`.
machine_only.vertical_generator_housing_from_conversi: The other half, and the only route to `powergrid:vertical_generator_housing`.
machine_only.generator_commutator_from_conversion: One half of a 2-cycle with `generator_vertical_commutator_from_conversion`, and a second route to `powergrid:generator_commutator`.
machine_only.generator_vertical_commutator_from_conve: The other half, and the only route to `powergrid:generator_vertical_commutator`.

duration._reason: Ticks per recipe, by the Factorio category the source surface maps to. A vanilla grid recipe carries no duration, so one has to be chosen; it is here rather than in the converter because CLAUDE.md's rule is that nothing is decided in the script. These match the pack's own emitted hand recipes, which sit at 10-20 ticks. Re-costing the grid line against Factorio's own timings is a later ticket's.
